subject: c12-math

weightage.label: Relations and Functions + Inverse Trigonometry (Ch 1 to 2)

note: Marks are official and given per unit (theory total 80, internal assessment 20). CBSE gives no chapter-wise weightage and says to cover all chapters. Question mix: remembering and understanding 44 marks (55%), applying 20 (25%), analysing, evaluating and creating 16 (20%).
mistakes: Calculus is 35 of 80 marks. Practise differentiation and integration rules regularly, and do not forget +C in indefinite integrals.
When you change the variable in a definite integral, change the limits too, or go back to the original variable.
Inverse trigonometric functions: use the principal value ranges when writing answers.
Matrices and determinants: AB is not always equal to BA, and cofactor signs alternate. Check the order before multiplying.
Vectors: do not mix up the dot product (a number) and the cross product (a vector). In 3D, keep direction ratios and direction cosines apart.
Linear programming: shade the feasible region carefully and test every corner point in the objective function.
Probability: define your events clearly before using Bayes' theorem or conditional probability.
Show every step of your working, so you can earn method marks even if the final answer is wrong.
order: Chapters 1 and 2 first (8 marks): they are the base for later chapters.
Chapters 3 and 4 (10 marks): matrices and determinants.
Calculus, Chapters 5 to 9 (35 marks): give this the most time and keep practising daily.
Vectors and 3D Geometry, Chapters 10 and 11 (14 marks).
Linear Programming, Chapter 12 (5 marks): a short chapter to revise before the exam.
Practise past-style questions with full written working, not only reading.
